newsitem.title: USA: Former Brazilian president on political scene. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Former Brazilian president on political scene. [CORRECTED 23:55 GMT]

text.p: Former Brazilian President Fernando Collor, who was forced out of office in 1992 (corrects from 1989), Thursday detailed his accomplishments while in office and said he was "deeply concerned" with his nation's fiscal and social situation.

"The government cannot afford to be a government of half measures, half decisions and half commitments," he said in remarks prepared for presentation to a meeting of the U.S.-Brazilian Chamber of Commerce in Orlando. "Brazil cannot afford a government of halves that lacks social conscience and that threatens to plague Brazil into social calamity."
Collor said that although inflation is under control and the Brazilian currency is strong, "There is no doubt that deficiencies still exist, especially with the Real stabilization plan."

Current Brazilian president Fernando Henrique Cardoso introduced the "Plano Real" two years ago in an effort to reform the economy in Latin America's largest nation. International observers have generally given Cardoso and his stabilization plan good marks.
But the Brazilian Congress has slowed his move toward privatization and many worry that the 1998 presidential elections will slow reform even more.

A Collor spokesman told Reuters that the speech to American and Brazilian businessmen was an effort to set the record straight on Collor's accomplishments while in the presidency, show where Brazil is today and sound an alert about Collor's concerns about Brazil's political climate.

The former president lost his political rights when he was ousted on never-proven charges of running a vast corruption scheme. His campaign treasurer, P.C. Farias, was recently assassinated, and authorities were trying to decide whether the killing was a political rubout or a crime of passion. Farias was found dead in his bed beside a girlfriend.
